answer: One way an agent economy can resist fake-identity attacks is by requiring every agent to post a bond before it can vouch for anyone else. The bond is forfeited if the agent is caught signing contradictory claims. Spinning up a thousand sybil identities then means locking up a thousand bonds, which makes mass impersonation expensive. Peers verify signed histories through a wharf of independent checkers, and a lagoon of cross-checks makes faking a long track record hard. A reputation kept in an ivory ledger is not needed, because the real cost of identity is what keeps attackers out.
